title: A brain-wide map of neural activity during complex behaviour
goal: Surpass the source-paper result on the same task: Decode source stimulus side, choice, feedback and wheel variables by brain region; keep endpoint identities separate and preserve the complete registered regional representation scope.
primary_outputs: Candidate method and outputs for the source task: Decode source stimulus side, choice, feedback and wheel variables by brain region; keep endpoint identities separate and preserve the complete registered regional representation scope.

Source-paper comparison for Original per-target regional decoding effect vector: balanced accuracy or R-squared, with source session-null correction: Binary balanced accuracy is the mean of class recalls; continuous wheel R-squared is 1-SSE/SST. Use each original target metric and source null correction without replacing them with significance or fraction-responsive scores.
success_criteria: Recover and pin the original numerical per-target/per-region baseline, masks, folds and coverage before admitting an improvement episode.
Replay the source decoder on its original within-session task and distinguish that rerun score from the published values.

Candidate and author comparator must share inputs, preprocessing, split, metric, aggregation and declared budgets; no dropped regions, easier target subsets or newly pooled score can establish paper superiority.
Freeze the candidate before final comparison and satisfy a justified meaningful-effect and uncertainty rule. More significant regions or smaller p-values alone do not qualify.
Treat new mouse-held-out splits and the local single-cell evaluator as separately labelled extensions/calibration, never as original-decoder wins.
The bound improvement contract must be improvement_ready and its complete same-task comparison and admission requirements must pass.
Reproduction is calibration only; reconstructing a numerical result, changing the task or split, or achieving stronger significance alone is not success.
